'''Geoffrey Richard Grimmett''' (born 20 December 1950)<ref name="whoswho">{{Who's Who | author=Anon| title=Grimmett, Prof. Geoffrey Richard | id = U18289 | year = 2014 | doi =10.1093/ww/9780199540884.013.U18289 | edition = online [[Oxford University Press]]|location=Oxford}}</ref> is an English mathematician known for his work on the mathematics of random systems arising in [[probability theory]]<ref name="random">{{Cite book | title=Probability and Random Processes | first2=D. R. | last2=Stirzaker | first1=G. R. | last1=Grimmett | year=2001 | publisher=Oxford University Press|isbn=0198572220}}</ref><ref name="graphics">{{Cite book | title=Probability on Graphs|url=http://www.statslab.cam.ac.uk/~grg/books/pgs.html  | first1=G. R. | last1=Grimmett | year=2010 | publisher=Cambridge University Press|isbn=978-0521147354}}</ref><ref name="Aldous2013">{{cite journal|last1=Aldous|first1=David|title=Book Review: ''Probability on graphs: random processes on graphs and lattices'' by Geoffrey Grimmett|journal=Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society|volume=51|issue=1|year=2013|pages=173–175|issn=0273-0979|doi=10.1090/S0273-0979-2013-01428-9|doi-access=free}}</ref> and [[statistical mechanics]], especially [[percolation theory]]<ref>{{Cite book | doi = 10.1007/978-3-662-03981-6_1| chapter = What is Percolation?| title = Percolation| pages = 1–31| year = 1999| last1 = Grimmett | first1 = G. | series = Grundlehren der mathematischen Wissenschaften| volume = 321| isbn = 978-3-642-08442-3}}</ref> and the [[Contact process (mathematics)|contact process]].<ref name="statslab">{{cite web | title=Geoffrey Grimmett's homepage at the University of Cambridge | url=http://www.statslab.cam.ac.uk/~grg/ }}</ref><ref name="googlescholar">{{Google scholar id}}</ref> He is the [[Professorship of Mathematical Statistics, University of Cambridge|Professor of Mathematical Statistics]] in the [[Statistical Laboratory, University of Cambridge]], and was the [[Master (college)|Master]] of [[Downing College, Cambridge]], from 2013 to 2018.<ref name="scopus">{{Scopus id}}</ref>

==Education==
Grimmett was educated at [[King Edward's School, Birmingham]] and [[Merton College, Oxford]]. He graduated in 1971, and completed his [[Doctor of Philosophy|DPhil]] in 1974<ref name="dphil">{{cite thesis |degree=DPhil |first=Geoffrey |last=Grimmett |title=Random Fields and Random Graphs |publisher=University of Oxford |date=1974 |url=https://copac.jisc.ac.uk/id/23497625?style=html |id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.457489}} |oclc=500458360 |author-link=Geoffrey Grimmett |access-date=16 September 2018 |archive-date=17 September 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180917034304/https://copac.jisc.ac.uk/id/23497625?style=html |url-status=dead }}</ref> under the supervision of [[John Hammersley]] and [[Dominic Welsh]].<ref name="mathgene">{{MathGenealogy|id=50997}}</ref>

==Career and research==
Grimmett served as the [[IBM]] [[Research Fellow]] at [[New College, Oxford]], from 1974 to 1976 before moving to the [[University of Bristol]].<ref name="whoswho"/><ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1016/0166-218X(85)90059-9| title = The shortest-path problem for graphs with random arc-lengths| journal = Discrete Applied Mathematics| volume = 10| pages = 57–77| year = 1985| last1 = Frieze | first1 = A. M. | last2 = Grimmett | first2 = G. R. | doi-access = free}}</ref> He was appointed [[Professorship of Mathematical Statistics, University of Cambridge|Professor of Mathematical Statistics]] at the [[University of Cambridge]] in 1992, becoming a fellow of [[Churchill College, Cambridge]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.admin.cam.ac.uk/reporter/2008-09/special/03/2.html|title=Fellows of the Colleges: Churchill|publisher=University of Cambridge|work=Cambridge University Reporter|date=2 October 2008|access-date=7 May 2009}}</ref> He was Director of the [[Statistical Laboratory, University of Cambridge|Statistical Laboratory]] from 1994 to 2000, Head of the [[Department of Pure Mathematics and Mathematical Statistics]] (DPMMS) from 2002 to 2007, and is a trustee of the [[Rollo Davidson Prize]].<ref>{{cite web | title=Trustees of the Rollo Davidson Trust | url=http://www.statslab.cam.ac.uk/Rollo/trustees.html | access-date=7 May 2009 | archive-date=29 September 2008 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080929135020/http://www.statslab.cam.ac.uk/Rollo/trustees.html | url-status=dead }}</ref>

Grimmett is particularly recognised for his achievements in the rigorous theory of disordered physical systems.<ref name=royal/> Especially influential is his work on and around [[percolation theory]], the contact model for stochastic spatial epidemics, and the random-cluster model, a class that includes the [[Ising model|Ising]]/[[Potts model]]s of [[ferromagnetism]].<ref name=royal/> His monograph on percolation is a standard work in a core area of probability, and is widely cited.<ref name=royal/> His breadth within probability is emphasized by his important contributions to probabilistic [[combinatorics]] and probabilistic [[number theory]].<ref name="royal"/>

In October 2013 he was appointed [[Master (college)|Master]] of [[Downing College, Cambridge]], succeeding [[Barry Everitt (scientist)|Barry Everitt]].<ref name="dow">[https://www.cam.ac.uk/news/new-master-elected-for-downing-college Professor Geoffrey Grimmett elected as next Master]</ref> He ended his term as Master on 30 September 2018, being replaced by [[Alan Bookbinder]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.dow.cam.ac.uk/news/downing-college-announces-master-elect|title = Downing College announces Master Elect|date = 29 November 2017}}</ref>

He was appointed Chair of the [[Heilbronn Institute for Mathematical Research]] in September 2020.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://heilbronn.ac.uk/2019/09/06/new-chair/ | title=Heilbronn Institute for Mathematical Research &#124; New Chair}}</ref> He was succeeded by [[Catherine Hobbs]] on September 1 2023.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://heilbronn.ac.uk/2023/02/20/new-chair-himr/ | title=Heilbronn Institute for Mathematical Research &#124; New Chair}}</ref>

==Awards and honours==
Grimmett was awarded the [[Davidson Prize|Rollo Davidson Prize]] in 1989<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.statslab.cam.ac.uk/rollo-davidson-awards-1976-2023|title=Rollo Davidson Awards 1976 – 2023|publisher=University of Cambridge Statistical Laboratory|access-date=2024-04-19}}</ref> and elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] (FRS) in 2014.<ref name="royal">{{cite web|title=Professor Geoffrey Grimmett FRS|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/geoffrey-grimmett-11547/|publisher=[[Royal Society]]|website=royalsociety.org|location=London|author=Anon|date=2014|access-date=2014-05-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180611075651/https://royalsociety.org/people/geoffrey-grimmett-11547/|archive-date=2018-06-11}} One or more of the preceding sentences incorporates text from the royalsociety.org website where: {{blockquote|"All text published under the heading 'Biography' on Fellow profile pages is available under [[Creative Commons license|Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License]]." --{{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161111170346/https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/|title=Royal Society Terms, conditions and policies|date=2016-11-11}}}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Grimmett is the son of Benjamin J Grimmett and Patricia W (Lewis) Grimmett.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.freebmd.org.uk/cgi/information.pl?cite=sBvu2l%2BeQ8rYa7%2F25ae8%2FA&scan=1|title=Index entry|access-date=10 May 2014|work=FreeBMD|publisher=ONS}}</ref>

He competed at the [[1976 Summer Olympics]] in [[Montreal]] as a member of the [[Great Britain]] Men's [[Foil (fencing)|Foil]] Team, finishing 6th.<ref>{{cite web|title=SR/Olympic Sports |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/gr/geoffrey-grimmett-1.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121020223007/http://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/gr/geoffrey-grimmett-1.html |archive-date=20 October 2012 }}</ref>
